event_text: The Paris Metro opens to passengers.
British colonies federate to form the Commonwealth of Australia.
Britain and Japan sign the Anglo-Japanese Alliance.
Revolutionary Gotse Delchev is killed fighting the Ottoman army.
Chekhov's play The Cherry Orchard premieres at the Moscow Art Theatre.
The Canadian provinces of Alberta and Saskatchewan are established.
The All-India Muslim League is founded in Dhaka.
Oklahoma becomes a U.S. state.
King Carlos of Portugal and his heir are shot dead in Lisbon.
note: regnal number dropped

event_text: The Brazilian football club Sport Club Internacional is founded in Porto Alegre.
Charles Rolls dies in an aeroplane crash at Bournemouth.
The Northern Territory and the Australian Capital Territory join the Commonwealth of Australia.
France makes Morocco a protectorate through the Treaty of Fes.
The United States Soccer Federation is formed.
The Maritz Rebellion of Boers against the Union of South Africa begins.
The Zimmerwald Conference begins in Switzerland.
Britain and France conclude the secret Sykes-Picot Agreement.
The Japanese city of Ōmuta is officially established.
note: founder name in the bullet looks like vandalism; left out

event_text: Prince Frederick Charles of Hesse is elected King of Finland.
The Treaty of Saint-Germain is signed, dissolving the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
note: clause added so it is not confused with older treaties of Saint-Germain

event_text: Warren G. Harding defeats James M. Cox for President of the United States.
The International Hydrographic Bureau is established under the League of Nations.
The Hollywood Bowl open-air music venue opens.
TIME magazine publishes its debut issue.
A Soviet-backed communist coup attempt fails in Estonia.
The Grand Ole Opry radio show debuts on WSM in Nashville.
Éamon de Valera founds the Fianna Fáil party in Ireland.
Juan Trippe founds Pan American World Airways.
Warlord Zhang Zuolin is killed by Japanese agents in the Huanggutun incident.
Wings wins the top film award at the Academy Awards ceremony.
The papal encyclical Casti connubii on marriage is issued.
note: regnal number dropped

event_text: The George Washington Bridge over the Hudson River is dedicated.
The BBC Empire Service begins shortwave radio broadcasting.
The Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States is signed.
Hitler becomes Führer of Germany after President Hindenburg dies.
The Hanshin Tigers baseball club is founded in Osaka, Japan.
The film Modern Times premieres in New York City.
note: "Modern" is part of the film's title

event_text: The airship Hindenburg bursts into flames at Lakehurst, New Jersey.
France's state railway company SNCF is created by merger.
The Soviet Union sets up the Finnish Democratic Republic puppet state.
British sailors free prisoners from the German tanker Altmark in Norwegian waters.
note: war label dropped

event_text: Franklin D. Roosevelt opens the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
Germany test-flies the Messerschmitt jet fighter using only its jet engines.
note: aircraft number dropped

event_text: King Boris of Bulgaria dies under suspicious circumstances.
note: regnal number dropped

event_text: Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg sign the customs convention creating Benelux.
The Allied Control Council formally takes power over occupied Germany.
Hungary formally abolishes its long-vacant monarchy and becomes a republic.
note: "long-vacant" separates it from the earlier Hungarian republic

event_text: The Constitution of Japan goes into effect.
The International Union for the Protection of Nature is founded in France.
The Soviet-led economic bloc Comecon is established.
India's constitution takes effect and the country becomes a republic.
The Festival of Britain opens in London with the Royal Festival Hall.
note: regnal number dropped

event_text: Princess Elizabeth becomes Queen of the United Kingdom.
The Academy Awards ceremony is held partly at New York's NBC International Theatre.
note: only ceremony held at that theatre

event_text: West Germany beats Hungary to win the World Cup in Bern.
A crash at the Le Mans motor race kills many spectators.
The Hungarian Revolution against the pro-Soviet government breaks out.
Haakon dies and his son Olav becomes King of Norway.
note: regnal numbers dropped; a medieval Haakon-to-Olav succession also exists

event_text: The United States launches Vanguard, a solar-powered satellite.
note: separates it from later Vanguard satellites

event_text: Hawaii is admitted as a U.S. state.
Dahomey (Benin) gains independence from France.
Tanganyika gains independence from the United Kingdom under Julius Nyerere.
John Glenn orbits the Earth in a Mercury spacecraft.
note: spacecraft name dropped (it contains a number)

event_text: NASA launches astronaut Gordon Cooper on a solo Mercury orbital mission.
The Forth Road Bridge opens in Scotland.
Canada adopts the maple leaf flag.
The FIFA World Cup tournament begins in England.
Ilse Koch, the Witch of Buchenwald, dies by suicide in prison.
Robert F. Kennedy is shot at the Ambassador Hotel in Los Angeles.
Meredith Hunter is stabbed to death at the Altamont Free Concert.
Japan launches the satellite Ohsumi on a Lambda rocket.
Sierra Leone becomes a republic.
Watergate burglars are arrested at the Democratic National Committee offices.
India launches the tiger conservation program Project Tiger.
A Turkish Airlines jet from Paris to London crashes, killing everyone aboard.
note: flight number dropped

event_text: Madagascar's president Richard Ratsimandrava is assassinated.
The Soweto uprising begins in South Africa.
Jimmy Carter signs the law creating the U.S. Department of Energy.
Iranian troops fire on protesters in Tehran on Black Friday.
Nazi criminal Josef Mengele drowns while swimming in Brazil.
John Lennon is murdered outside his New York City apartment building.
MTV launches as a round-the-clock music video channel.
Chariots of Fire wins Best Picture at the Academy Awards.
War breaks out between Sudan's government and the Sudan People's Liberation Army.
wording_source: article lead: Second Sudanese Civil War
note: separates it from the earlier Sudanese civil war

event_text: A gunman kills people at a McDonald's in San Ysidro, San Diego.
The Australian soap opera Neighbours debuts on television.
Jeltoqsan protests break out in Soviet Kazakhstan.
The Brundtland Commission publishes its report Our Common Future.
Pakistan's president Zia-ul-Haq dies in a plane crash.
Soviet troops kill demonstrators at a rally in Tbilisi, Georgia.
The Rwandan Patriotic Front invades Rwanda from Uganda, starting a civil war.
The Unrepresented Nations and Peoples Organization is founded in The Hague.
A Sicilian Mafia car bomb kills judge Paolo Borsellino.
Members of Austria's Freedom Party split off to form the Liberal Forum.
Palau gains independence from a United Nations trusteeship.
Quebec voters narrowly reject independence from Canada in a referendum.
note: "narrowly" separates it from Quebec's earlier referendum

event_text: A Birgenair charter jet crashes into the Atlantic off the Dominican Republic.
note: flight number dropped

event_text: Armored bank robbers fight police in the North Hollywood shootout.
The European Central Bank is established.
The Santer Commission of the European Union resigns over corruption allegations.
Real Madrid beats Valencia to win the UEFA Champions League.
Apple releases its Mac operating system codenamed Cheetah.
note: version name dropped (it contains a numeral)

event_text: NASA launches the Aqua Earth-observing satellite.
The Canal Hotel bombing in Baghdad kills UN envoy Sérgio Vieira de Mello.
NASA launches the MESSENGER probe to study Mercury.
Tony Blair's Labour wins a British general election with a sharply reduced majority.
wording_source: article lead: 2005 United Kingdom general election
note: separates it from Blair's other election wins

event_text: NASA launches the New Horizons probe to Pluto.
European Union members sign the Treaty of Lisbon.
ESA launches the Jules Verne cargo spacecraft to the International Space Station.
note: separates it from later cargo spacecraft of the same type

event_text: An earthquake devastates L'Aquila, Italy.
An Airblue passenger jet crashes near Islamabad, killing everyone aboard.
note: flight number dropped

event_text: A bomb kills Coptic Christians leaving a church in Alexandria, Egypt.
Felix Baumgartner skydives from the stratosphere in the Red Bull Stratos jump.
Countries sign the Minamata Convention to limit mercury pollution.
Knife-wielding attackers kill many people at Kunming railway station in China.
Al-Shabaab gunmen kill students at Garissa University College in Kenya.
Italian voters reject a constitutional referendum and Matteo Renzi resigns.
Kim Jong-nam, half-brother of Kim Jong-un, is killed with a nerve agent.
Turkey launches a military offensive against Kurdish forces in Afrin, Syria.
In Estonia's parliamentary election, Reform stays largest as the Conservative People's Party surges.
note: separates it from other Estonian elections
